before: Starting from the Beckey-Tate approach, the route traverses hard right across overlaps to reach a big ledge below an open-book corner. From there it climbs two classic, clean corner pitches — the second through a burly bulge at 5.11c, the route's crux — followed by a wide-crack section, then exits via easier cracks to the top of the wall.

Located 30 meters right of the Kearney-Thomas start, this variation climbs solid granite splitters and left-facing corners (5.10+) before trending left into a right-facing corner, then joins the Kearney-Thomas line and finishes via a 5.11 finger-crack variation.

before.notes: Straight off the ground up a splitter layback crack in the golden granite of the central south face.

Crosses blank granite on seven bolts to reach the main crack. First done at A1 with tension moves, later freed at 5.11. The wall below the big roofs is vertical to overhanging, with seams that often lead nowhere.

A committing aid pitch on bird beaks, hooks and tipped-out cams, climbing to the base of the large roof system called the Kangaroofs. The last pitch with drilled anchors; everything above is natural gear. Pendulum attempts right from here found only seams.
Aid up a corner that cuts through the roof, with about 400 ft of air below. Small wires in the roof corner are marginal, and a fall here is into space.
Aid out the next roof. Placements are marginal. A fall here can go past the belay, so protect the rope from sharp edges.
Above the roofs, the upper wall eases into free climbing up cracks, dihedrals and chimneys on natural gear, topping out near 8,300 ft. No one has recorded per-pitch grades for this section.

before: 2 rappels, both on a single 30 m rope: one off the summit block to the base of the boulder move, then scramble to the top of the lower pitch and rappel to the ridge

before.name: SR-20 Pullout / Willow Creek approach start
before.directions: From the summit of Washington Pass, drive SR-20 east about 3.5 miles and park in the long pullout on the right side of the road at about 4,320 ft, where the Willow Creek valley opens up toward Big Snagtooth.

before.name: Big Snagtooth Summit
before.directions: Drop southeast through trees about 120 ft to Early Winters Creek and cross on a log near the mouth of Willow Creek. Climb steeply up the north side of Willow Creek, often brushy, until the slope eases near 5,000 ft, then continue into the upper basin near 7,000 ft. Turn south up about 400 ft of loose scree or snow to the west-ridge saddle, scramble the crest to the summit block, and climb the short chimney and friction slab to the top.
